system:
You read documents filed on a United States court docket, OCR'd to markdown, for
a research dataset of contract clauses.

An INSTRUMENT is a document whose text the parties negotiated and by which they
bound each other: a contract, agreement, policy, lease, deed, guaranty, note,
plan, bylaws, handbook, amendment, or similar. Hallmarks: recitals, defined
terms, numbered operative sections, an execution or signature block.

A FILING is a document made for the court: complaint, answer, motion, brief,
memorandum, order, affidavit, declaration, notice, docket sheet, certificate of
service, civil cover sheet.

THE DECISIVE RULE. A filing that **attaches** an instrument counts — report the
instrument's own boundaries, not the filing's. A filing that merely **quotes** an
instrument does not count at all: a brief reproducing three sentences of an
agreement is a filing, and the file contains no instrument.

WHAT IS NOT AN INSTRUMENT, even when signed or filled in: a blank or fill-in
form; an agency certificate or registration; an exhibit index; a declarations
page or coverage-summary table; a schedule of rates or fees standing alone; an
invoice, receipt or statement of account. These record or summarise; the parties
did not negotiate their text.

WHAT IS NOT A PROVISION: a heading on its own; a title page; a table of
contents; a signature, notary or attestation block; an exhibit index. A
provision states an obligation, right, grant, limitation, condition or
definition. Give the range of the operative text, including its heading.

LIST EVERY SUBSTANTIVE PROVISION, in document order. Do not skip any. Do not
judge whether a provision is well or badly drafted. Do not rank them.

The file is given to you with a line number and a `│` at the start of every line.
Line numbers are not part of the text; they are how you point at it.

OCR REPAIR. For each provision you must also give its text. Copy it verbatim
from the lines you named, then repair only what the scanner broke: words split
across a line break, words run together, `l`/`1` and `O`/`0` confusions, stray
table pipes and cell debris, page numbers and Bates stamps sitting inside the
text. Do not paraphrase, modernise, reorder, summarise, or drop anything. Never
change a number, an amount, a date, or a cross-reference. Never add or remove a
word — a repair that deletes `not` inverts the clause. If a passage is too
damaged to repair honestly, copy it as it stands.

Add nothing of your own: no `[struck through: ...]`, no `[sic]`, no
`[illegible]`, no explanatory brackets of any kind. Executed contracts are often
marked up by hand, and the OCR shows deleted wording as `~~struck~~`. Reproduce
those words as plain text, in place, and say what you saw in the repairs
sentence instead.

   33│# **VERIFIED COMPLAINT FOR INJUNCTIVE RELIEF, DECLARATORY JUDGMENT, NEGLIGENCE AND NUISANCE**
   34│
   35│For its Verified Complaint against Defendant Roy D. Mercer, L.L.C. ("Defendant"), Plaintiff BNSF Railway Company ("BNSF") states as follows:
   36│
   37│## **PARTIES, JURISDICTION AND VENUE**
   38│
   39│1. BNSF is a Delaware corporation authorized to transact and do business in the State of New Mexico.
   40│2. BNSF owns and operates railroad facilities in Socorro County, New Mexico.
   41│3. Defendant is a New Mexico limited liability company and owns certain real property located in Socorro County, New Mexico.
   42│4. The Court has jurisdiction over these proceedings pursuant to Article VI, Section 13 of the New Mexico Constitution.
   43│5. Venue is proper in this Court pursuant to NMSA 1978, § 38-3-1 in that the property which is the subject of this action lies in Socorro County.
   44│
   45│## **GENERAL ALLEGATIONS**
   46│
   47│6. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 5 of the Complaint.
   48│
   49│ 
   50│
   51│
   52│
   53│
   54│
   55│7. BNSF owns and operates an approximately 2,190 miles of transcontinental railroad that provides high-volume, efficient ground transportation of freight to and from ports of Southern California to Chicago, Illinois.
   56│
   57│8. As part of this railroad system, BNSF owns and operates railroad track and facilities in Socorro County, New Mexico. A portion of these facilities is located adjacent to a tract of land owned by Defendant which lies within a silting basin for the Brown a/k/a Mantanza Arroyo (hereinafter referred to as the "Brown Arroyo Property"). A plat depicting BNSF's railroad facilities and the Brown Arroyo Property is attached as Exhibit A.
   58│
   59│9. The Brown Arroyo is located south of the City of Socorro, and drains an entire watershed basin consisting of approximately 42 square miles of land east of the Magdalena Mountains. The arroyo flows in the easterly direction towards the railroad tracks and is considered a tributary of the Rio Grande with a gauge station that measures its flow.
   60│
   61│10. The Brown Arroyo Property is located within Sections 30 and 31, Township 3 South, Range 1 East, N.M.P.M, Socorro County, New Mexico. The Brown Arroyo Property consists of a number of Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District ("MRGCD") tracts—Tracts 4 through 7, 9 and 10 (as shown on MRGCD Maps 165 and 166)—and is situated between BNSF's tracks and the Luis Lopez Community Ditch, south of the City of Socorro. A full legal description of the Brown Arroyo Property is attached hereto as Exhibit B.
   62│
   63│✓ 11. Defendant acquired the Brown Arroyo Property by deed filed in the Office of the County Clerk of Socorro County on December 29, 2003. *tracts 479 & 10*
   64│
   65│12. Upon information and belief, in the mid 1930s, the Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District ("MRGCD") owned all or most of the tracts of land of which the Brown Arroyo Property consists, as well as other adjacent property now owned by BNSF.
   66│
   67│13. Certain deeds into MRGCD, including at least one conveying a tract which is now subsumed within the Brown Arroyo Property, recite that MRGCD acquired title to the land “for right-of-way for the Brown Arroyo control.”
   68│
   69│14. By Easement dated September 23, 1936, MRGCD granted to BNSF’s predecessor, The Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company, a right of egress and ingress onto MRGCD Tracts 2-10 in Sections 19, 20 and 31 shown on District Map 165 and Tracts 1 and 8A in Section 31 on Map No. 166 “for the purpose of excavating, constructing and maintaining” a “surface ditch, dykes and spoil banks, together with any other facilities or structures necessary or desirable for the protection of the railroad or other property of [the railroad]” from waters flowing down the Brown Arroyo. The tracts referenced in the Easement include the Brown Arroyo Property.
   70│
   71│15. In addition to the rights of egress and ingress, the Easement grants BNSF the right “to use so much of the natural material as such earth, rock, wood, etc. as it may elect or desire to remove for the purpose of constructing” the ditch, dykes, spoil banks, and other necessary facilities and structures to protect the railroad from the floodwaters of the Brown Arroyo.
   72│
   73│16. Upon information and belief, the diversion system was built in the mid to late 1930s to control floodwaters flowing down the Brown Arroyo.
   74│
   75│17. The diversion system begins on BNSF property adjacent to its track where the original flow of the arroyo is diverted 90 degrees by a system of levees, dykes and channel that parallels the track. The system extends south off of BNSF’s property, onto the Brown Arroyo Property, then onto other private land, and then back onto BNSF property where the channel elbows to the east and passes underneath BNSF’s bridge at the railroad’s milepost 981.3. The diversion system is approximately 2 miles in length.
   76│
   77│18. BNSF and its predecessors have historically maintained the diversion system, rebuilding the levees and dykes after breaches caused by floodwaters, entering upon privately owned property.
   78│
   79│✓ 19. Between July 27, 2006 and August 6, 2006, unprecedented, extraordinary rainfall events caused extreme flooding throughout Socorro County.
   80│
   81│20. The extraordinary rainfall caused water flowing down the Brown Arroyo to breach the diversion levees in several locations and washed-out BNSF's track and roadbed.
   82│
   83│21. The breaches in the roadbed caused BNSF to cease operations for short-periods of time while the tracks and roadbeds were cleared and repaired.
   84│
   85│22. The County, Socorro Electric Cooperative, Inc., Middle Rio Grande Conservancy District, the City of Socorro, the Army Corps of Engineers, federal Bureau of Land Management and BNSF all participated in meetings to discuss short term and long term solution to repair flood damaged property and prevent future damage from storm water flooding. Soon after the breaches occurred, BNSF's contractors, in coordination with Socorro County and other task force members and at the considerable expense of BNSF, worked to rehabilitate the diversion system, clearing vegetation, building up the levees, expanding the diversion channel, and constructing piers to control floodwaters to minimize the likelihood of additional breaches and flood damage. Some of the rehabilitation work was done on the Brown Arroyo Property.
   86│
   87│✓ 23. In or about November 2006, Defendant notified BNSF of a claim that BNSF trespassed on the Brown Arroyo Property when rehabilitating the diversion system. Since notice of Defendant's claim, the parties have sought to resolve the dispute without resort to litigation.
   88│
   89│24. By email dated May 19, 2008, counsel for Defendant stated that unless the matter is resolved by May 30, 2008, Defendant will mobilize earthmoving equipment and commence
   90│
   91│the removal of the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property on June 3, 2008. The May 19, 2008 email is attached hereto as Exhibit C.
   92│
   93│25. Removal, interference with, or modification of the diversion system, which is specifically designed to control the high volume of floodwaters of the Brown Arroyo, will likely result in the wash out of BNSF's tracks, the flooding of adjacent landowners' property and will significantly interfere with the interstate railroad system.
   94│
   95│## **FIRST CLAIM FOR RELIEF** (Temporary Restraining Order/Preliminary Injunction)
   96│
   97│26. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 25 of the Complaint.
   98│
   99│27. Defendant's threatened conduct of destroying the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property will expose BNSF's property and operations to a significant risk of injury from floodwaters flowing down the Brown Arroyo.
  100│
  101│28. Unless Defendant's threatened conduct as described herein is restrained now and later enjoined on a preliminary and permanent basis, BNSF will suffer immediate and irreparable injury and harm for which there is no adequate remedy at law.
  102│
  103│29. The equity and hardships between BNSF and Defendant support issuance of a temporary restraining order and a preliminary injunction prohibiting Defendant from removing, interfering with or modifying the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property.
  104│
  105│30. BNSF seeks to maintain the *status quo* with respect to the diversion system which has been located on the Brown Arroyo Property for approximately 70 years.
  106│
  107│31. A bond should not be required of BNSF because Defendant will not suffer any sudden harm or damage if it is prevented from removing or otherwise interfering with the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property.
  108│
  109│32. There is a substantial likelihood that BNSF will prevail upon a trial on the merits in this matter.
  110│
  111│## **SECOND CLAIM FOR RELIEF** (Permanent Injunction)
  112│
  113│33. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 32 of its Complaint.
  114│
  115│34. Defendant's threatened conduct as described herein will cause BNSF irreparable harm for which there is no adequate remedy at law.
  116│
  117│35. The equity and hardships between BNSF and Defendant support issuance of a permanent injunction prohibiting Defendant from removing, interfering with, or modifying the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property.
  118│
  119│36. BNSF seeks to maintain the *status quo* with respect to the diversion system which has been located on the Brown Arroyo Property for approximately 70 years.
  120│
  121│## **THIRD CLAIM FOR RELIEF** (Declaratory Judgment – Express Grant of Easement)
  122│
  123│37. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 36 of its Complaint.
  124│
  125│38. BNSF is the holder of an express easement which allows it the right of egress and ingress onto the Brown Arroyo Property, and the right to use of natural materials on the Brown Arroyo Property to construct and maintain the diversion system.
  126│
  127│39. Defendant had either actual, constructive, or inquiry notice of the grant of easement.
  128│
  129│40. An actual and justiciable controversy has arisen and now exists between BNSF and Defendant concerning BNSF's right to enter and use the Brown Arroyo Property for the
  130│
  131│construction and maintenance of the diversion system. BNSF is entitled to judicial declaration by this court pursuant to the New Mexico Declaratory Judgment Act, NMSA 1978, §§ 44-6-1 to 44-6-15 and Rule 1-057 NMRA that BNSF is the holder of an express easement on the Brown Arroyo Property for the use of constructing and maintaining a diversion system to control floodwaters flowing down the Brown Arroyo.
  132│
  133│## **FOURTH CLAIM FOR RELIEF** (Declaratory Judgment – Prescriptive Easement)
  134│
  135│41. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 40 of its Complaint.
  136│
  137│42. Upon information and belief, BNSF and its predecessor AT&SF have maintained the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property openly, uninterruptedly, peaceably, notoriously, adversely and under a claim of right for more than ten (10) years.
  138│
  139│43. Defendant and its predecessors in interest had actual or constructive knowledge of the adverse, open, uninterrupted and continuous use of the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property.
  140│
  141│44. An actual and justiciable controversy has arisen and now exists between BNSF and Defendant concerning BNSF's right to enter and use the Brown Arroyo Property for the construction and maintenance of the diversion system. BNSF is entitled to judicial declaration by this court pursuant to the New Mexico Declaratory Judgment Act, NMSA 1978, §§ 44-6-1 to 44-6-15 and Rule 1-057 NMRA that BNSF is the holder of a prescriptive easement on the Brown Arroyo Property for the use of constructing and maintaining a diversion system to control floodwaters flowing down the Brown Arroyo.
  142│
  143│## **FIFTH CLAIM FOR RELIEF**
  144│
  145│(Declaratory Judgment – Implied Easement by Necessity or Estoppel)
  146│
  147│45. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 44 of its Complaint.
  148│
  149│46. Land owned by BNSF and the Brown Arroyo Property are contiguous and were previously owned by MRGCD.
  150│
  151│47. Severance of the Brown Arroyo Property and the land now owned by BNSF curtailed access of BNSF to and from the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property.
  152│
  153│48. A reasonable necessity existed for the diversion system at the time the BNSF land and the Brown Arroyo Property were severed.
  154│
  155│49. The Brown arroyo has been located on the Brown Arroyo Property, and maintained by BNSF and its predecessor AT&SF, with the knowledge of, and without objection from, Defendant's predecessors in interest for approximately 70 years.
  156│
  157│50. An actual and justiciable controversy has arisen and now exists between BNSF and Defendant concerning BNSF's right to enter and use the Brown Arroyo Property for the construction and maintenance of the diversion system. BNSF is entitled to judicial declaration by this court pursuant to the New Mexico Declaratory Judgment Act, NMSA 1978, §§ 44-6-1 to 44-6-15 and Rule 1-057 NMRA that BNSF is the holder of an implied easement by necessity or estoppel on the Brown Arroyo Property for the use of constructing and maintaining a diversion system to control floodwaters flowing down the Brown Arroyo.
  158│
  159│## **SIXTH CLAIM FOR RELIEF**
  160│
  161│(Negligence)
  162│
  163│51. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 49 of its Complaint.
  164│
  165│52. Alternatively, if BNSF does not have a right to enter the Brown Arroyo Property to maintain and rehabilitate the diversion system, Defendant is responsible for maintenance of the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property so that the floodwaters of the Brown Arroyo are allowed to flow unimpeded to the river. Defendant failed to maintain the diversion system, allowing it to essentially dam the floodwaters so that they breached BNSF's roadbed.
  166│
  167│53. As owner of the Brown Arroyo Property, Defendant has a duty to maintain the floodwater diversion system in such condition to enable them to flow down the Brown Arroyo and be delivered under BNSF's bridge in a manner that would not foreseeably injure BNSF.
  168│
  169│54. Defendant breached its duty of care by failing to maintain the diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property, and such failure was the proximate cause of damages to BNSF
  170│
  171│55. BNSF's damages include its loss of business due to cessation of operations occasioned by breach of its roadbed property and the costs incurred to repair its tracks and roadbed and to rebuild and repair the diversion system, and any other damages flowing from Defendant's breach of duty.
  172│
  173│## **SEVENTH CLAIM FOR RELIEF** (Nuisance)
  174│
  175│56. BNSF incorporates by reference as though fully set forth herein paragraphs 1 through 54 of its Complaint.
  176│
  177│57. Alternatively, if BNSF does not hold an easement on the Brown Arroyo Property, Defendant's failure to maintain the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property created a nuisance that resulted in damages to BNSF.
  178│
  179│58. Defendant's failure to maintain the diversion system caused an invasion of flood waters onto BNSF's property, and such invasion was unreasonable and interfered with BNSF's private use and quiet enjoyment of its property.
  180│
  181│59. Defendant's actions and omissions have resulted in damages to BNSF including loss of business due to cessation of operations occasioned by flooding of its property and the costs incurred to repair its tracks and roadbed and to rebuild and repair the diversion system, and any other damages flowing from Defendant's conduct.
  182│
  183│WHEREFORE, BNSF respectfully requests the Court to award the following relief:
  184│
  185│A. Enter a Temporary Restraining Order restraining Defendant Roy Mercer, L.L.C. and its agents, servants, employees and attorneys from removing, interfering with, or modifying the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property and from interfering with the efforts of BNSF or its agents or contractors to maintain the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property.
  186│
  187│B. Following a hearing in this case, enter a preliminary injunction prohibiting Defendant and its agents, servants, employees and attorneys from removing, interfering with, or modifying the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property and from interfering with the efforts of BNSF or its agents or contractors to maintain the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property.
  188│
  189│C. Following a trial in this case, enter a permanent injunction prohibiting Defendant and its agents, servants, employees and attorneys from removing, interfering with, or modifying the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property and from interfering with the efforts of BNSF or its agents or contractors to maintain the floodwater diversion system on the Brown Arroyo Property in the future.
  190│
  191│D. Declare that BNSF owns an easement on the Brown Arroyo Property for use as a floodwater diversion system.
  192│
  193│E. Alternatively, in the event that BNSF is determined not to have a right to enter on the Brown Arroyo Property to maintain the floodwater diversion system, award BNSF its actual and consequential damages in an amount to be determined at trial for the loss of business occasioned by flooding of its property, costs incurred to clear and repair its tracks and roadbed and to rebuild and repair the diversion system, and other damages to be proven at trial.
  194│
  195│F. Recovery of prejudgment and post-judgment interest on any amounts due BNSF.
  196│
  197│G. Recovery of BNSF's costs of suit.
  198│
  199│H. Such other and further relief this Court deems just and proper.
